name: Mike Beltran
bio: Mike Beltran is a Tampa Bay-area attorney who represented District 70 in the Florida House of Representatives from 2018 to 2024. Born in New York City, he holds degrees from the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard Law School. He is the Republican nominee for Florida's 14th Congressional District.

platform.point: Expand telehealth access and remove regulatory barriers to opening new clinics so families can see doctors closer to home.
Cut taxes, pointing to sales-tax holidays and a large Florida tax cut he backed in the legislature.
Reduce regulations he says hold back business growth and worker advancement.
Oppose new data center development that lacks local approval and environmental safeguards.
Challenge career politicians who, in his view, put party loyalty ahead of constituents.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on tax cuts and tax holidays and on reducing business regulation.

liberty.evidence: State House record includes anti-abortion legislation (restrictive) and an open-carry firearms bill (permissive), plus youth vaping limits.

education.evidence: Endorsed by school-choice organizations during his legislative career.

notes: Education score rests on endorsements rather than a stated policy.

name: Brian Lambert
bio: Brian Lambert is a retired U.S. Navy sailor who served 20 years, including work as an aviation structural mechanic, flight engineer and intelligence specialist at U.S. Central Command in Tampa. He entered the Navy from Georgia in 1998. He is the Libertarian nominee for Florida's 14th Congressional District.

platform.point: Protect earned benefits, cut VA bureaucracy, widen community care access and address veteran suicide.
Balance the federal budget, cut waste and restrain spending to limit debt on future generations.
Lower taxes and reduce regulation on small businesses and entrepreneurs.
Increase patient choice and price transparency while reducing federal involvement in medicine.
Secure borders and ports of entry while supporting legal immigration.
Give parents more authority over schooling and avoid one-size-fits-all federal approaches.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower taxes, less regulation and cutting federal spending.

welfare.evidence: Favors patient choice and less federal interference in health care.

liberty.evidence: Guns: pledges to protect the right to bear arms without compromise; no stated position on abortion, drugs or speech.

immigration.evidence: Wants every border secured while supporting legal immigration.

education.evidence: Emphasizes parental empowerment alongside support for teachers.

notes: Campaign headshot URL inferred from the site's image optimizer path. Liberty score rests on the gun issue only.

name: Laurel Lee
bio: Laurel Lee has represented Florida in the U.S. House since 2023 and serves on the Energy and Commerce, Judiciary and House Administration committees. She previously was Florida Secretary of State (2019-2022), a Hillsborough County circuit judge, and a federal prosecutor and public defender. She holds undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Florida.

platform.point: Supported border wall funding and a larger Border Patrol workforce, and backs anti-human-trafficking measures.
Make tax relief permanent, including the small-business deduction, a larger child tax credit and no tax on tips and overtime.
Draw on prosecutorial experience to oppose lenient crime policies and fund DNA testing under the Debbie Smith Act.
Improve absentee voting for deployed troops and expand mental health care and job placement for veterans.
Balance AI innovation with consumer protection and intellectual property safeguards through her work on the House AI task force.

economy.evidence: Supports lower, flatter taxes, spending cuts and permanent extension of tax relief.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: opposes it except to save the mother's life; guns: calls the Second Amendment an individual right; LGBTQ: says gender identity is not a protected class.

security.evidence: Led the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act reauthorizing FISA Section 702; supports qualified immunity.

immigration.evidence: Voted for border wall funding and more Border Patrol agents; served as a Mayorkas impeachment manager.

energy.evidence: Supports fracking and says environmental regulations cost jobs.

tech.evidence: Introduced the bipartisan DEFIANCE Act on non-consensual deepfake images and serves on the House AI task force.

faith.evidence: Says religious liberty is at risk and supports religious exemptions from vaccination requirements.

notes: Several OnTheIssues positions date from her 2022 campaign.

name: Robert People
current_role: Retired U.S. Army sergeant first class
bio: Robert People served 21 years in the U.S. Army (1997-2018) as an ammunition specialist and Army journalist, with deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. Born in Baltimore, Maryland, he won the August 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 15th Congressional District.

platform.point: Enact Medicare for All, treating health care as a right, and fund more women's health research.
Raise the cap on income subject to Social Security tax to protect benefits.
Expand clean energy investment, restore EPA standards and address rising electricity rates.
Create faster pathways to citizenship and guarantee due process; lists abolishing ICE as a top priority.
Ban members of Congress from trading stocks.
Refuse AIPAC money and oppose further arms shipments to Israel.

economy.evidence: Proposes raising the Social Security payroll tax cap and banning congressional stock trading.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and free school meals for all children.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: decisions belong to a woman and her doctor; LGBTQ: supports transgender health care access.

immigration.evidence: Backs faster citizenship pathways and due process, and lists abolishing ICE among his top priorities.

foreign.evidence: Opposes further arms shipments to Israel.

energy.evidence: Supports expanding clean energy, ending fossil fuel favoritism and restoring EPA standards.

education.evidence: Proposes cost-of-living-based minimum teacher salaries and universal free school meals.

notes: Welfare raised from 65 to 90 because his platform explicitly calls for Medicare for All.

name: Sydney Gruters
current_role: Former executive director of the New College Foundation
bio: Sydney Gruters was vice president of advancement and executive director of the New College Foundation in Sarasota. She previously served as district director for U.S. Rep. Greg Steube, worked for U.S. Rep. Vern Buchanan, and was Florida state director for USDA Rural Development. She is the Republican nominee for Florida's 16th Congressional District.

platform.point: Cut taxes and regulations to make everyday essentials more affordable for families.
Work with President Trump and ICE on enforcement against illegal immigration.
Address overdevelopment to keep homeownership within reach.
Protect Social Security and Medicare and improve veterans' benefits.
Strengthen election integrity measures.

economy.evidence: Pledges to cut taxes and regulations and pursue conservative responses to inflation.

immigration.evidence: Pledges to work with President Trump and ICE to enforce immigration law.

notes: Earlier liberty score of 80 was cleared because the cited abortion pledge could not be found on the current campaign site and the news source was paywalled. She is endorsed by the Faith & Freedom Coalition of Florida.

name: Kelly Kirschner
bio: Kelly Kirschner is a third-generation Floridian and a former Sarasota city commissioner and mayor. He served in the Peace Corps in Guatemala, led the nonprofit UnidosNow, and was a vice president at Eckerd College. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees from Georgetown University.

platform.point: Create a federal insurance backstop, negotiate drug prices, expand affordable housing and limit Wall Street home buying.
Ban offshore drilling and open-water fish farming and strengthen Clean Water Act enforcement.
Reverse Medicaid and Medicare cuts and protect coverage for pre-existing conditions.
Close corporate tax loopholes and address tax avoidance by billionaires.
Require congressional debate before wars of choice and end open-ended overseas spending.
Fully staff the VA and restore round-the-clock Veterans Crisis Line service.

economy.evidence: Calls for closing corporate loopholes, taxing billionaire avoidance and negotiating drug prices.

welfare.evidence: Wants Medicaid and Medicare cuts reversed and pre-existing condition protections kept.

foreign.evidence: Wants congressional debate before wars of choice and an end to open-ended overseas spending.

energy.evidence: Supports banning offshore drilling and stronger Clean Water Act enforcement; endorsed by the Sierra Club.

tech.evidence: Would block AI data centers until their environmental safety is demonstrated.

notes: Tech score rests on his data center stance, which is framed mainly as an environmental issue.

name: Mark Davis
current_role: Air Force veteran and small-business owner
bio: Mark Davis served in the U.S. Air Force from 2005 to 2013 and later worked in corporate retail operations management. He lives in Parrish, Florida, and is running without party affiliation in Florida's 16th Congressional District.

platform.point: Adopt universal health care that covers everyone instead of employer-based or profit-driven plans.
Oppose tariffs and pursue policies to address rising rents, insurance costs and stagnant wages.
Support reproductive freedom and common-sense gun regulations.
Handle immigration and crime with practical policies that respect civil liberties.
Improve services and benefits for veterans.

welfare.evidence: Supports universal health care covering everyone.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports reproductive freedom; guns: supports gun regulations.

immigration.evidence: Rejects 'invasion' framing and calls for immigration policy that respects liberty.

notes: The campaign image may not be a formal headshot.

name: Greg Steube
bio: Greg Steube has represented Florida in the U.S. House since 2019, after serving in the Florida House (2010-2016) and Florida Senate (2016-2018). He is a U.S. Army veteran who served as a JAG Corps captain, including in Iraq. A Sarasota resident, he holds undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Florida.

platform.point: Lower business taxes and replace the current tax code with a flat tax.
Repeal the Affordable Care Act in favor of market-based health insurance.
Build a border wall and oppose sanctuary cities.
Sponsored the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act restricting transgender athletes in federally funded programs.
Support private school vouchers and keep education decisions with the states.
Advance conservative principles and the America First agenda.

economy.evidence: Supports lower business taxes and a flat tax.

welfare.evidence: Supports repealing the ACA and prefers market-based insurance to government coverage.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: opposes it except for the mother's life; guns: opposes more gun control; LGBTQ: sponsored the transgender sports bill.

security.evidence: Favors stricter crime prevention while keeping existing police accountability rules.

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall, opposes sanctuary cities and wants those here illegally to leave and reenter legally.

foreign.evidence: Voted for a moratorium on Ukraine aid and puts U.S. sovereignty ahead of the UN.

energy.evidence: Opposes government climate regulation and backed repealing Florida's cap-and-trade program.

education.evidence: Supports vouchers for private schools and state control of education.

faith.evidence: Emphasizes Judeo-Christian values in government and supports student inspirational messages in schools.

notes: He introduced bills to limit tech platforms' suspension of accounts, which does not map cleanly onto the tech scale.

name: Matthew Montavon
bio: Matthew Montavon is a retired planner from suburban Sarasota who worked in local government planning and managed a department at the UN Food and Agriculture Organization in Rome. He co-founded the Suncoast Immigration Justice Coalition and is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 17th Congressional District after an earlier unsuccessful primary run.

platform.point: Offer affordable housing incentives, homeowners insurance relief and transparent health care pricing.
Prefers a government-supported single-payer system while remaining open to private options.
Modernize border security and create legal-status pathways for agriculture, hospitality and construction workers.
Secure federal money for transportation, water management and Gulf Coast storm resilience.
Restore congressional authority over executive orders and audit federal programs to cut redundancy.

economy.evidence: Supports ending tax breaks for the wealthy and federal support for housing and daycare.

welfare.evidence: Prefers single-payer health care and opposes SNAP and Medicaid cuts.

immigration.evidence: Opposes deporting long-term residents and says ICE should be reformed or abolished.

notes: Two campaign domains appear in search results (montavonforcongress.com and montavon4congress.com); the latter did not load. Social accounts are listed on the site but exact URLs were not confirmed.

name: Michael Quirk
bio: Michael Quirk is a no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 17th Congressional District in the November 2026 general election.
notes: No campaign website, biography or policy statements were found.

name: Scott Franklin
bio: Scott Franklin has served in the U.S. House since 2021, representing FL-15 and then FL-18 since 2023, and sits on the Appropriations Committee. He spent 26 years in the U.S. Navy as a naval aviator, later led the Lanier Upshaw insurance agency, and served on the Lakeland City Commission. He was born in Georgia.

platform.point: Lower taxes and reduce federal spending to encourage economic growth.
Lists standing up for Christian values among his campaign priorities.
Strengthen national security and reduce reliance on China.
Support a border wall and immigration bans from countries that do not cooperate.
Protect constitutional rights and oppose socialism.

economy.evidence: Supports lower taxes, corporate tax cuts and decreased federal spending.

welfare.evidence: Opposed the 2022 Honoring our PACT Act expanding VA benefits for toxic-exposure veterans.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: pledges to vote against it; guns: voted against background checks for private transfers.

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall and immigration bans from non-cooperating countries.

foreign.evidence: Voted for aid to Israel after the 2023 Hamas attack and supports applying the 2002 Iraq AUMF to ISIS.

faith.evidence: His campaign lists standing up for Christian values as a core priority.

notes: Faith score is new and based on a campaign priority heading without detailed policy text.

name: Curtis Gibson
current_role: Former Lake Wales City Commissioner; mall manager and restaurant owner
bio: Curtis Gibson is a former Lake Wales city commissioner who manages Eagle Ridge Mall and owns a restaurant. He is a former professional wrestler and has lived in Lake Wales for over 20 years. He is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 18th Congressional District.

platform.point: Create a federal reinsurance backstop to stabilize the market and lower homeowner premiums.
Cut VA delays and ensure local care or clear routes to covered local providers.
Seek property tax relief for homeowners, seniors and working families.
Help citrus growers with replanting and protect farms from development pressure and disease.
Bring federal road and safety funding to the Heartland and hold projects accountable for delays.
Hold local town halls and publish monthly public updates.

notes: His issues page focuses on local concerns that do not map clearly onto the ten scales.
